incidents.root_cause: Valid native-command STDERR was treated as PowerShell failure under Windows PowerShell 5.1.
incidents.prevention: Determine native command success from LASTEXITCODE; capture or redirect STDERR deliberately.

incidents.root_cause: Empty gh JSON output was not normalized before existence logic.
incidents.prevention: Normalize null/empty to an empty array and assert count before property use.

incidents.root_cause: A collection of commit objects was cast to Int32.
incidents.prevention: Use array cardinality with @(...).Count or a documented numeric field.

incidents.root_cause: Remote PR merge success was treated as proof that local main/HEAD was normalized.
incidents.prevention: Discover local state and perform only an explicitly authorized ff-only normalization when needed.

incidents.root_cause: CLI JSON decoded to a nested array shape that was counted incorrectly.
incidents.prevention: Flatten/enumerate the decoded structure explicitly and assert resulting cardinality.

incidents.root_cause: A native/tool error message did not terminate the mutation loop as assumed.
incidents.prevention: Use explicit exit-code gates and verify destination inventory after mutation.

incidents.root_cause: Placeholder values were issued inside executable commands.
incidents.prevention: Issue only real values or first discover and assign them programmatically.

incidents.root_cause: A multi-line script block was executed interactively without its complete variable context.
incidents.prevention: Deliver multi-line executable content as a file; console receives only invocation lines.

incidents.root_cause: Validation relied on presentation/form artifacts rather than semantic/content evidence.
incidents.prevention: Verify decoded content, hashes, semantic names and independently verifiable artifacts.

incidents.root_cause: A signing configuration flag was treated as proof of signing capability; identity scope also drifted.
incidents.prevention: Prove signing with a detached signature or throwaway-repo commit; keep project identity local.

incidents.root_cause: Windows path manipulation was applied to a server-relative URL.
CLI option behavior was assumed and a stale downloaded script was executed.
incidents.prevention: Read local help, capture CLI version, verify downloaded script identity/content marker before execution.

incidents.root_cause: A global clean-worktree precondition ignored exact expected recovery artifacts already materialized with verified bytes.
incidents.prevention: Classify worktree entries as EXPECTED or UNEXPECTED before treating non-clean state as unsafe.

incidents.root_cause: Non-ASCII punctuation embedded in a Windows PowerShell 5.1 script was decoded incorrectly and caused a parser failure before execution.
incidents.prevention: Use ASCII-only PowerShell 5.1 source by default; prohibit smart punctuation; use ASCII-safe markers or encoded payloads for Unicode document content; byte-check final script before issuance.

incidents.root_cause: Semantic content was matched using an exact multiline string whose newline representation differed between the document and Windows PowerShell source.
incidents.prevention: Normalize EOL or use bounded semantic parsing/regex before multiline matching; assert exactly one intended match before mutation.

incidents.root_cause: Controlled-document self-status and registry lifecycle/authority metadata were allowed to evolve independently without a mechanical coherence gate; document mutation also requires explicit canonical register rebind verification.
incidents.prevention: Normalize recognized lifecycle-bearing self-status values and compare them with document-register lifecycle state; fail closed on contradiction or ambiguity; verify source_commit:path and canonical SHA-256 binding after controlled-document mutation.

incidents.root_cause: Three related script-generation failures violated native-tool and dependency-order contracts: CLI stdout and stderr were merged before JSON parsing; a Windows PowerShell automatic variable name was reused as a function parameter and altered gh invocation semantics; and a remote merge commit was used for local Git graph validation before the object had been materialized locally. A fourth failure showed that a Windows PowerShell 5.1 script was issued without a mechanical parser gate, allowing ambiguous expandable-string variable interpolation next to a colon to survive generation and fail at parse time before execution.
incidents.prevention: Parse structured CLI JSON from stdout only while preserving stderr as diagnostics; treat PowerShell automatic/reserved runtime variable names as prohibited identifiers for script parameters and mutable state; distinguish remote ref visibility from local object availability and fetch/prove required objects before local graph validation; recovery remains discovery-first before repeating any authorized mutation. Require a zero-error Windows PowerShell 5.1 parser gate before issuance, and prohibit ambiguous expandable-string interpolation next to syntactically significant characters unless explicitly delimited or formatted.
